question: Should OpenClaw pursue distributed job orchestration as a core Gateway feature, a plugin-provided backend/API seam, or documented external orchestration while the narrower cron, session, runtime, and federation trackers proceed separately?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but backend ownership, queue semantics, config shape, failure/retry/dead-letter behavior, observability, and dependency/security posture require maintainer product and architecture intent.

options.title: Design Backend-Neutral Orchestration
options.body: Define shared scheduler/job ownership, worker claiming, retries, dead-letter, and observability contracts first, then decide whether Redis/BullMQ is one implementation behind that seam.

options.title: Split Into Narrow Tracks
options.body: Keep this issue as prior art while cron HA, external session storage, distributed runtime, and federation issues each own their narrower implementation choices.

options.title: Document External Orchestration
options.body: Decide not to add a core backend for now and document safe external queue or scheduler patterns around OpenClaw deployments.

recommendation.title: Design Backend-Neutral Orchestration
recommendation.body: Define shared scheduler/job ownership, worker claiming, retries, dead-letter, and observability contracts first, then decide whether Redis/BullMQ is one implementation behind that seam.
